review.reviewer: Codex implementation owner (self-review, not independent approval)
review.decision: Keep a bounded recent Codex parse snapshot instead of discarding a large session cache entirely
review.notes: Read-only current-session measurements found300 turns/~25.8MB serialized, cold Load1.77s and a repeat1.16s; source retains up to800 turns then drops a cache entry above32MiB. New code must bound retention while streaming and across append resumes, keep full individual turn content and original ordinals/record IDs, expose omitted prefix via existing count/cursor contracts, and keep source history recoverable. No real-session mutation, transcript copy, cache-limit increase or production deployment. Existing cache/history tests stay unchanged. Current-session timing is not a synthetic benchmark or device/UI acceptance; the first /usr/bin/time wrapper returned1 only because sandbox denied sysctl after the probe finished, and a direct rerun exited0; preserve both records.

cases.description: Large Codex history keeps a bounded reusable recent cache and lossless source history access
cases.setup: Isolated Codex rollout with enough complete public turns to exceed the existing32MiB retention budget, a fresh Loader and exact source-based history cursor; no real HOME/session data
cases.action: Read newest turns twice unchanged, append a complete turn then reread, and page into the omitted prefix using the source history API
cases.expected: After the first read a cache entry remains within32MiB and an unchanged read reuses that entry rather than rescanning; latest public prompt/response/tool data, original ordinal and record identity remain exact. Appended input extends the cached active turn safely and preserves prior returned snapshots; retained budget remains bounded. Earlier source turns are still readable by valid cursor and no source bytes are changed. A single individually oversized turn stays complete even if it cannot be cached. Old implementation must fail the large-entry-retained assertion, not a timeout/compile/setup assertion.
